Marie (People Ops): Heads up 0 I was on partial unpaid leave for two days in Jan and payroll still took a 401(k) deferral on the 1/15 check. Can that be undone so I don't hit an excess deferral?
Alex (Payroll): @Marie DM your employee ID + paydate and I'll take a look. If the money hasn't hit the custodian we can reverse; once invested the custodian usually needs to do a corrective distribution.
Marie (People Ops): DM'd emp 024578 + paydate 2026-01-15. Also noticed an employer pro-rated HSA contribution posted 1/31 1 will that change my HSA year limit? I planned to increase my own pre-tax deduction starting Feb.
Jamal (Benefits): Short version: employer HSA deposits count toward the annual HSA maximum. We'll reconcile employer + employee amounts. For the 401(k), we need custodian confirmation whether they invested on 1/19 per payroll file. If invested, custodian corrective distribution is the standard route.
Alex (Payroll): Payroll records show ACH to plan clearing on 2026-01-18 and custodian posted 2026-01-19. I'll ask custodian for their corrective distribution steps.
benefits-bot: Please upload the paystub/remittance using /upload-benefits-file in #people-ops. Attach transaction confirmation if available.
Marie (People Ops): Uploaded remittance + paystub.
Jamal (Benefits): If custodian issues corrective distribution they'll return the excess deferral plus investment earnings. The excess deferral portion is taxable in the year contributed; earnings are reported on Form 1099-R. If payroll can reverse before investment, that avoids 1099-R complexity.
Marie (People Ops): If custodian returns the excess, will I get a 1099-R and need to amend anything else? Concerned about surprises at tax time.
Chris (Tax): If you receive a corrective distribution, the deferral portion should be included in taxable wages for the year contributed (might show on W-2), and the earnings portion is on 1099-R in the year distributed. We'll coordinate filings and provide suggested wording for your tax preparer.
Alex (Payroll): Custodian responded: funds invested 2026-01-19, they will process a corrective distribution; ETA 7 business days. I'll post the dollar amount once they confirm.
Marie (People Ops): Thanks. For the HSA, if employer+employee exceed the IRS limit because of that pro-rated deposit, what's the remedy and timeline? Don't want penalties.
Jamal (Benefits): Options: 1) request a return of excess HSA contribution from the custodian (they return amount + earnings), or 2) adjust remaining employee contributions to avoid exceeding the limit. We'll run the numbers and advise.
Lina (Finance): I'll review payroll/custodian paperwork once Alex posts the corrective distribution amount to determine if any W-2 adjustments are needed this tax year.
Alex (Payroll): Will loop Tax/Finance and post custodian confirmation here.
Marie (People Ops): Appreciate it  happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.
benefits-bot: Reminder: update your HSA election in Workday after changing deferral percentages to keep YTD contributions accurate.
